text: What does the JVM's just-in-time compiler do?
choices: Interprets bytecode one instruction at a time forever
Compiles the whole program before it starts
Converts Java source directly to machine code
Compiles frequently executed methods to native machine code while the program runs
explanation: It interprets at first while watching, then compiles hot methods natively. This is why a Java program is slow for its first few thousand iterations and abruptly faster afterwards — and why any benchmark that ignores warm-up is worthless.
